chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Do not jest, or your light will dissipate. Do not lie, or your splendour will dissipate. Beware of two traits: restlessness and laziness. For if you are restless, you will not be able to bear a responsibility patiently; and if you are lazy, you will not fulfill a right.

He said: And the Messiah (peace be upon him) used to say: Whoever's worries multiply, his body becomes ill. Whoever's character worsens, his soul suffers. Whoever's speech multiplies, his errors multiply. Whoever's lying multiplies, his splendour dissipates. Whoever disputes men excessively, his chivalry dissipates.

key_terms.بهاء: Baha' (splendour/dignity) -- the outward manifestation of inner virtue and spiritual grace
key_terms.ضجر: Dajar (restlessness/impatience) -- agitation that prevents steadfastness in fulfilling duties
key_terms.مروءة: Muru'ah (chivalry/manly virtue) -- the complete set of noble qualities expected of a person of character
key_terms.نور: Nur (spiritual light) -- a divine radiance that illuminates the believer's face and heart, lost through frivolous behavior

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about jesting, lying, and laziness?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delivers a concise exhortation against jesting, lying, restlessness, and laziness, warning that these vices destroy a person's spiritual light, dignity, patience, and ability to fulfill obligations. He then quotes Jesus the Messiah (AS) -- a figure revered as a prophet in Islamic tradition -- who taught that excessive worry, bad character, excessive talk, lying, and quarreling each carry specific self-destructive consequences. This hadith was transmitted in the scholarly circles of Qom through a well-documented chain of narrators.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Hashim from `Ubaydullah b. `Abdullah al-Dahqan from Darast b. Abi Mansur from `Abdullah b. Sinan.

He said: Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq (a.s.) said: Do not jest, or your light will dissipate. Do not lie, or your splendour will dissipate. Beware of two traits: (1) restlessness, and (2) laziness. If you are restless, you will not be able to bear a responsibility patiently; and if you are lazy, you will not be able to fulfill the right [of another].

He said: The Messiah (as) would say: He whose worries multiply, his body becomes ill. He who worsens his character, his soul suffers. He whose speech multiplies, his errors multiply. He whose lying multiplies, his splendour dissipates. He who disputes men excessively, his chivalry dissipates.
